headline: No risk-based allocation or volatility-management rule beats buying and holding SPY after California taxes with good confidence. None of the 258 unlevered configs beats SPY in any regime. That covers vol targeting, risk parity / min-variance / max-diversification / HRP / risk budgets, CPPI, drawdown tiers, vol-scaled momentum and a vol-target overlay on the incumbent: they cut drawdowns and sometimes raise the Sharpe ratio, but they cost about 0.5-9 pp/yr. Levered vol targeting with SSO does beat SPY over 2006-2026 (CA with tax-aware execution: score +3.40 pp, full +4.85 pp, boot_p 0.011; NONE: +4.64 pp, boot_p 0.010), but only through about 1.7-1.8x leverage. In CA the gain budget freezes it into near-constant ~1.9x leverage, and a never-rebalanced 50% SPY / 50% SSO scores the same (+3.39 pp). On synthetic 2x history (2000-2026 and 1986-2026) it fails the bar (boot_p 0.26-0.35, Sharpe below SPY's, max drawdown -79%), and the family's walk-forward is negative in CA, so nothing passes.
findings: Scope: 558 configs ran (454 family search configs, the multiple-testing count; 104 hindsight-check configs), giving 1022 (config, regime, protocol) results on the screen/full/long_screen/long protocols. The first researcher's 637 cached results were reused unchanged because the module was not edited. Their planned 753-config screen was cut by the battery throttle: 213 grid configs ran in full plus a 56-config representative subset of the RP/CPPI/DD/VM/OV/filter groups.

Unlevered vol targeting of SPY (146 configs, 2000-2026): before tax it works as advertised. Median max drawdown is -40% vs SPY's -55%, and in NONE 86% of configs raise the Sharpe ratio (median +0.03, matched-vol +0.5 pp). But return falls: median score -1.06 pp/yr in CA and -0.76 in NONE; best CA +0.03 and best NONE +0.50 (boot_p 0.46). In CA most of the Sharpe gain is gone (median -0.005) because de-risking sales realize gains. Tax-aware execution brings it back to about zero (best CA +0.14, boot_p 0.77) by suppressing trades. Power-2 (Moreira-Muir), 200-day trend and VIX term-structure filters all lowered the score.

Risk parity / min-var / max-div / HRP / risk budgets lose to SPY in every regime: SPY+VUSTX -1.4 to -1.7 pp/yr (CA), SPY+TLT -2.3 to -2.5, with gold -3.3 to -3.9, the global 8-asset menu -5.6 to -7.7. Risk-adjusted they look best: SPY/TLT/GLD min-variance has a NONE Sharpe of 0.88 vs 0.67 and +3.2 pp matched-vol. Levered RP via SSO/UBT/UGL (2010-2026) still lost 1.1-2.1 pp/yr in NONE and 3.0-3.6 in CA. ERC on 40 random BROAD_POOL_2003 menus lost by a median 3.0-5.5 pp/yr (79 of 80 menu x regime cases negative). Removing GLD changes nothing.

CPPI lost 3.0-5.0 pp/yr (CA). Drawdown-tier de-risking lost 0.05-0.8 (CA) and cut the max drawdown to -34% to -43%. Vol-scaled momentum lost 3.5-8.6. Tax-executed inverse-vol momentum on the incumbent's 22 ETFs scored -0.36 (CA). The tax-executed vol-target overlay on the incumbent's rotation scored CA -0.18 with full +1.53 pp and boot_p 0.056 on the full protocol: Sharpe 0.57 vs SPY's 0.42 and volatility 12.5%. The incumbent scores +0.66 / +1.54 / boot_p 0.025 with Sharpe 0.51. The overlay is a smoother incumbent, not a better beat-SPY strategy (10y beat 60%).

Levered vol target (SPY+SSO, exposure = 25%/21d vol, cap 2x), full protocol 2006-07..2026: in NONE score +4.64, full +4.33, all 10-year windows ahead (worst +2.92), boot_p 0.010, Sharpe 0.71 vs 0.67, max drawdown -55% (= SPY). Average exposure is 1.66x. The 1.5x-capped version scores +3.18 (boot_p 0.012, Sharpe 0.72, matched-vol +0.79).
With plain execution in CA the same levered signal is taxed away: score +0.83, full +0.38, boot_p 0.40 (FED +1.78, boot_p 0.19). Its 1986-2026 synthetic analogue scores -0.18 in CA (long protocol).

With tax-aware execution (SPY/IWB/VTI + SSO/DDM, lots chosen by tax cost, 1%/yr realized-gain budget) the CA score is +3.40, full +4.85, 10y beat 98%, 15y beat 100%, boot_p 0.011, max drawdown -61%; FED +3.64 and NONE +4.01. That clears bar items 1-3 on the SSO-era sample. But the gain budget freezes the exposure: average 1.82x, about 1.9x every year since 2010 for the 2006 start, and stuck near 1.35x for a 2019 start. It is a path-dependent constant-leverage portfolio. Matched-vol excess is only +0.12 pp. Constant 1.5x, 1.8x and 2x and the never-rebalanced 50/50 SPY/SSO score +3.4 to +6.0 with drawdowns of -71% to -85%.

Longer history with cost-calibrated synthetic 2x funds (research-only) shows the leverage dependence. The CA lead's 2000-2026 analogue scores +2.31 with boot_p 0.35 (Sharpe 0.36 vs 0.42). The 1986-2026 long protocol gives +2.46, 10y beat 74%, 15y beat 72%, boot_p 0.26, max drawdown -79%; the pre-2000 holdout is positive (ho5 +5.8). The NONE lead's 1986-2026 analogue passes items 1-3 (+2.68, 81%/92%, boot_p 0.057), but its Sharpe is below VFINX's (0.55 vs 0.57) and its max drawdown is -65%.

Cross-underlying hindsight check: the same levered rule on DIA/MDY/IWM/EFA/EEM/QQQ (synthetic 2x) beats its own index's buy-and-hold only for high-Sharpe indexes. In NONE: QQQ +4.80, DIA +2.97, MDY +0.83, IWM -0.81, EFA -0.72, EEM -2.30, with Sharpe below the index's own on 5 of 6. With tax-aware execution in CA it loses on IWM/EFA/EEM, with drawdowns of -63% to -83%. Its success is a bet on the levered index's equity premium.

Overfitting diagnostics (screen family). In CA the walk-forward is negative: 10y->5y -0.53 pp and 5y->3y -1.26 pp with the lab's default steps; 10y->5y -1.42 pp (25% of 12 decisions) with yearly steps. PBO is 0.002 only because leverage dominated every sub-sample. The deflated Sharpe of the best config is 0.002, and the verification battery gives the CA lead a DSR of 0.067. In NONE the walk-forward is -2.89 / -1.59 pp, PBO 0.145.

Verification battery for the CA lead: robust to costs (CA score +3.62 / +3.11 / +2.24 at 0 / 15 / 35 bps per side). Stricter yearly distribution-tax accounting moves the excess little (from 2006: +4.85 -> +4.59). Sub-periods: CA 2010-2020 +2.50, 2020-2026 +3.36. Rebalance-offset and lag tests do not apply to the custom kind.

hindsight_checks: (1) The levered SPY vol target uses the benchmark index itself, so there is no star instrument to remove. The hindsight risk is the decision to lever the US large-cap index after its best era. Check (a): the same levered rule (25% target, 2x cap) ran on the six other indexes that have cost-calibrated synthetic 2x series: DIA, MDY, IWM, EFA, EEM, QQQ. Each was compared with its own buy-and-hold on the screen protocol from 2000-2004. This set is fixed and predefined because synthetic 2x exists only for these, so it is not a random draw. In NONE the rule beats its own index on QQQ (+4.80 pp/yr), DIA (+2.97) and MDY (+0.83), and loses on IWM (-0.81), EFA (-0.72) and EEM (-2.30); its Sharpe is below the index's own on 5 of 6. In CA with plain execution it loses on 5 of 6. With tax-aware execution in CA: QQQ +4.92, DIA +2.71, MDY +0.23, IWM -1.28, EFA -1.77, EEM -3.37, with max drawdowns of -63% to -83%. Conclusion: the rule works only where the levered index had a high Sharpe, so it is a leverage bet on that index's equity premium. Check (b): synthetic 2x history extends the SPY rule to 2000 (CA lead boot_p 0.35) and to 1986 (CA lead 10y beat 74%, 15y beat 72%, boot_p 0.26; pre-2000 holdout +5.8 pp, positive). (2) Unlevered vol targeting (EWMA20, 18% target) on 20 random funds from BROAD_EQUITY_POOL_2003, each against its own buy-and-hold in NONE: the median score was -0.81 pp/yr with 3 of 20 positive. The Sharpe was higher on 10 of 20 (median +0.013), and the max drawdown was smaller on 19 of 20 and tied on 1. This matches the SPY result: lower risk, lower return. (3) Risk parity: removing the star GLD from the SPY/TLT/GLD, all-weather and global menus leaves every version losing 2.0-8.9 pp/yr. ERC on 20 random 6-fund menus from BROAD_POOL_2003 and on 20 random 4-equity + 2-bond menus lost to SPY in 79 of 80 menu x regime cases, by a median 3.0-5.5 pp/yr, with a Sharpe above SPY's in only 0-25% of menus. The hand-picked menus were no worse than random ones.
concerns: Every levered result rests on 2006-07..2026 for real SSO, a sample dominated by a post-2009 low-volatility bull market in which 1.5-2x S&P exposure was simply the right bet. Its one big de-risking win was 2008, and only for portfolios started before the crash. Synthetic extensions to 2000 and 1986 weaken it sharply.

Tax-aware vol targeting is path-dependent: the gain budget freezes the exposure at whatever level it had when gains accumulated. Results therefore depend on the start date relative to volatility regimes, so a new investor today would lock in about 1.9x leverage that cannot be de-risked without large realized gains. A crash after gains have built up would hit at close to 2x, with -79% to -85% drawdowns on synthetic history.

Synthetic 2x series (SYN_*2XC) are model-built and research-only: 2x total return, minus T-bills + 0.6%/yr financing, minus 0.9%/yr expense, calibrated to SSO within 0.1 pp/yr over 2006-2026. Pre-2006 financing and fund frictions may differ.

The engine does not enforce wash sales, and the family's tax-aware kind (like the lab's 'tax' execution) blocks only re-buys after a loss sale. For the CA lead's 2007 start, 21% of realized losses ($10.3k of $49.1k) came from loss sales within 30 days of a same-fund purchase. Under the real rule those losses would be deferred, so they are front-loaded in the backtest.
Leveraged ETFs (SSO, DDM, UPRO) carry daily-reset decay, about 0.9%/yr fees, swap financing and closure risk. The engine has no margin, so leverage can come only from these funds.

Not runnable on the website today: SSO, DDM, IWB and SHY are research-only tickers and risk_alloc.taxvt is a research kind. The risk-parity menus use research-only bond, gold and commodity funds such as VUSTX.

Compute throttling (battery) cut the first researcher's planned 753-config screen. RP/CPPI/DD/VM/OV and the vol-target filters were covered by a 56-config representative subset plus targeted sets, not the full grid. All 56 lost in CA, so a reversal elsewhere in the grid is unlikely but not proven.

The 1986+ tax-aware analogue uses a single 1x vehicle (VFINX). After a loss sale the 31-day re-buy block can leave it in cash, which may understate a multi-fund implementation. The 3-vehicle ETF-era synthetic test from 2000 also failed boot_p (0.35), so the conclusion does not hinge on this.

Engine distributions are taxed only at sale. The battery's stricter yearly accounting moved the CA lead's excess by only -0.01 to -0.26 pp, but bond-heavy risk-parity results are flattered by the engine; they lose anyway.

The pre-registered score and the first-start bootstrap reward different things. Constant leverage has a higher score than vol-targeted leverage, while the vol target wins boot_p only because the bootstrap uses the 2006-07 start's path, which includes the 2008 de-risking.
untested_ideas: Hedge-sleeve vol targeting for taxable accounts: keep a never-sold 1x core and de-risk by trimming a separate SSO sleeve or buying an inverse ETF (SH) with cash, so de-risking does not realize gains on the low-basis core. This needs a new signal in risk_alloc.py, which would have invalidated all cached results, so it was not done.
A wash-sale-correct tax-aware kind that also blocks loss sales within 30 days after a same-fund purchase, and re-scoring the CA lead with it.

The rest of the planned screening grid: RP lookbacks 21/126/252 on all menus; the all-weather (AW5), G6, US4, G7 and MF4 menus unlevered; 3x levered RP (UPRO/TMF); target-vol RP on more menus; more CPPI multipliers/floors and drawdown-tier shapes; time-series VM with blended lookbacks; UPRO 3x vol targets beyond the 2 that ran.
Long-history (1986+) runs of the 1.5x-capped NONE variant and of more tax-aware neighbours (only t0.20/c1.5, t0.30 and EWMA ran).

A neighbourhood of the tax-executed vol-target overlay on the incumbent rotation (targets 12-20%, vol lookbacks 21/126, monthly vs quarterly). Only one config ran; it gave a smoother incumbent (Sharpe 0.57 vs 0.51) but a negative score.
Leverage financed more cheaply than 2x ETFs (futures, box spreads, portfolio margin). This is not expressible in the engine.
Vol targeting with downside-semivariance or correlation-aware (multi-asset) scaling of the incumbent's top-5 holdings under the incumbent's tax-managed trade rule.
FED-specific tuning (only the finalists ran in FED); random-menu checks for tax-executed RP.
lab_bugs: report.diagnostics calls metrics.walk_forward with the default step_quarters=4 whatever the protocol. On the yearly 'screen' protocol that steps 4 starts, i.e. 4 years, leaving only 3 (10y->5y) or 4 (5y->3y) decision dates. The step should be 4 quarters, i.e. 1 start per year on screen. I report yearly-step results alongside.

metrics.monthly_matrix ends in .dropna(), so PBO (cscv_pbo) and the deflated Sharpe silently use only the months that every config covers. For this family that is 2011-01..2026-07, because a few levered risk-parity configs start in 2011. That drops 2000-2010, including 2000-02 and 2008, for all configs and is not reported in the diagnostics output.

The wash-sale guard in blocks.WeightStrategy 'tax' execution (copied by this family's TaxVT) only blocks re-buying a ticker within wash_days after a loss sale. It does not catch a loss sale within 30 days after a purchase of the same ticker, and the engine does not enforce wash sales, so harvested losses are front-loaded. Measured: about 21% of the CA lead's realized losses for a 2007 start.

registry.code_version hashes the source file that registers a signal (and core files) but not the files of signals it wraps. For example, risk_alloc.overlay with inner 'common.momentum' would keep stale cache entries if families/common.py changed.

metrics.summary takes bench_max_dd and bench_sharpe from the benchmark's run from the protocol's first start (2000-01), not from the config's own first start (2006-07 for SSO-based configs). Max drawdown is unaffected here because SPY's worst drawdown falls in both periods, but the engine-Sharpe comparison is misaligned for late-starting configs.
